findings.F1: The test's result points the way the idea predicts, but it is too weak to confirm: a short bet's unusual 10-day move is +1.36 % per case with t 1.51 on 310 cases over 227 days. The test already used all 19 coins on all four folds of daily data, so no more data is available to strengthen it.
findings.F2: In folds B and C, one window carries the effect.
findings.F3: The effect changes sign across periods rather than holding throughout.
findings.F4: The idea's grading is absent, so deeper falls are not followed by larger continuations.
findings.F5: The idea's deeper-fall grading does not reappear in other cuts.
findings.F6: Other horizons and the recent week do not sharpen the result.
findings.F7: Most of the unusual move comes from removing the coins' normal drift, not from the coins actually falling, and the book cannot pay.

no_ideas: The theme's effect is not in the data. The slide's continuation in an agitated choppy market rests on one window (w16; without it +0.42 %, t 0.20, F2), reverses in other windows and years (F3), and is not graded by the depth of the fall in any cut (F4, F5). No narrower case of the situation gives a clear answer, and no more data is available to test the idea unchanged (F1).
